technical-data.invention-title: COMPOSITIONS COSMETIQUES CONTENANT DE LA VITAMINE B3

abstract.p: Disclosed are cosmetic compositions including lipsticks, comprising from about 0.01 % to about 50 % by weight, of a crystalline vitamin B3 compound having an average particle size of from about 0.01 mu m to about 200 mu m; from about 1 % to about 90 %, b y weight, of an emollient component; and from about 1 % to about 90 % by weight, of a solidifying agent. The compositions provide improved skin feel of crystalline vitamin B3 compounds when applied to skin.

L'invention concerne des compositions cosmétiques, notamment des bâtons de rouge à lèvres, qui renferment: environ entre 0,01 % et 50 % en poids d'un composé de vitamine B3 cristallin avec une granulométrie moyenne variant approximativement entre 0,01 mu m et 200 mu m; environ entre 1 % et 90 % en poids d'un constituant émollient; et environ entre 1 % et 90 % en poids d'un agent solidifiant. Les composés de vitamine B3 cristallins de ces compositions offrent une sensation améliorée une fois ces dernières appliquées sur la peau.

description.p: The present invention relates to topical cosmetic compositions containing crystalline vitamin B compounds dispersed m an emollient or oil phase

Niacm, also known as vitamin B3, is the common name for nicotrnic acid The physiologically active form of niacm is macmamide. also a member of the vitamin B3 family of compounds Niacm and macmamide (nicot ic acid amide) function in the body as components of two coenzymes nicotmamide adenme dinucleotide (NAD) and nicotmamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP) Until recently, these vitamin B3 compounds were used exclusively to treat niacin deficiency and pellegra

Today, however, solubilized vitamin B3 compounds have also found use m the area of skm care actives Bπtish Patent 1,370,236 describes compositions for skm lightening containing 0 5% to 10% niacin Similarly, U S Patent 4,096.240 discloses the use of 0 1% to 10% macmamide for skm lightening Vitamin B3 compounds have also been found useful m regulating the texture of human skm See PCT application WO 97/39733, to Oblong et al

However, when applied to the skm in crystalline form (l e , powder), vitamin B3 compounds tend to impart a rough feel to the skin In the past, the crystalline vitamin B3 compounds were solubilized in a polar solvent before application to skm, thus alleviating the rough feel of the crystals However, solubilization reduced the efficacy of the vitamin B compound upon contact with the skm Thus there exists a need for cosmetic compositions comprising unsolubilized crystalline vitamin B3 compound(s) which provide improved consumer perceived sk feel The present inventors have discovered that cosmetic formulations incorporating the crystalline vitamin B3 compounds of specific particle size m combmation with an emollient, improve the consumer perceived feel of the crystalline vitamin B3 compound on the skin The present inventors have further discovered that these compositions are especially useful to impart vitamin B3 benefits to the lips with improved skm feel when used in lipstick compositions including a solidifying agent

It is, therefore, an aspect of the present invention to provide cosmetic compositions, preferably anhydrous cosmetic compositions, comprising crystalline vitamin B3 compounds which improve the appearance and feel of the skin while alleviating the rough feel of the crystalline vitamin B3 compound
Another aspect of the present invention is to provide cosmetic compositions compπsmg crystalline vitamin B3 compounds havmg reduced particle size

A further aspect of the present invention is to provide substantially anhydrous lip compositions such as lipsticks and lip-paints, compπsmg crystalline vitamin B3 compounds havmg reduced particle size

These and other aspects will become readily apparent from the detailed descπption which follows
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

All percentages, parts and ratios are based upon the total weight of the cosmetic compositions of the present mvention, unless otherwise specified All such weights as they pertam to listed mgredients are based on the active level and, therefore, do not include earners or by-products that may be mcluded in commercially available matenals, unless otherwise specified

The solubility of the vitamm B3 compound in the vanous non-polar emollients of the present mvention can be determined as follows
I Preparation of Samples for Analysis
1 ) the emollient is placed m pre-weighted vial and then saturated with a vitamin B3 compound,

2) the vial is shaken and allowed to sit in a bath at 30°C for 1 hour A small stir bar is used to agitate the contents of the vial If no precipitation occurs in the vial, then more macmamide is added This was repeated until precipitation occuned The sample is left m the bath for an additional 48 hours to insure saturation,
3) the saturated emollient is drawn mto a syringe,
4) A 045 micron filter (Gelman Acrodisc) is fitted on the end the syringe and the emollient is filtered through into separate pre- weighted vial for analysis,
5) The emollient is analyzed usmg HPLC to determine the amount of macmamide therem

Approximately 0 25g of the sample is weighed (sample weight) into a 15mL plastic screw-cap centnfuge tube The sample is mixed with approximately 3mL of 50/50 v/v methanol/chloroform and homogenized by vortex mixing About 7mL of water is then added to extract the vitamm B3 compound from the methanol chloroform phase Each sample is mixed by shaking 50 times m a back and forth motion to facilitate transfer of the macmamide from the methanol/chloroform to the water phase This
mixmg creates an emulsion at the mterface of the two phases. The emulsion can be dissipated by letting the sample stand for several hours or by bnef centnfugation (15 seconds) at high speed Once the two phases have completely separated, a pipette is used to carefully transfer the aqueous phase mto a separate, pre-weighted vial. The weight of the aqueous phase is noted (aqueous phase weight). An aliquot of the aqueous phase is transfened to an analysis contamer and analyzed for macmamide by HPLC (Waters 2690 Separations Module coupled with a Waters 996 PDA detector, both supplied by Waters Corporations). Ill.Calculations:

The percent vitamm B3 compound is determined by takmg the vitamin B3 compound concentration measured by HPLC and multiplying by the dilution factor. The dilution factor is the aqueous phase weight divided by the sample weight.
